title: Before Tuesday's open: will the bounce hold?
text: Monday was one of the best days in years. SPY rose 4.7% and QQQ rose 7.0%, led by a 31% jump in NVIDIA after its CEO came back. Early Tuesday, stock futures pointed lower. Futures are bets on where prices will open, so this hints that some people are taking profits. At the open, watch whether NVIDIA keeps most of its gain. A small step back after a giant day is normal. A big drop would show that investors are still nervous.

title: NVIDIA: back at the top, but questions remain
text: NVIDIA closed Monday at $165.05. It is still about 32% below its high of the past year ($243.37). Jensen Huang is CEO again, but the board's review is not finished. He has also agreed to answer questions from three House committees on December 1. New facts from either one could move the stock. Its risk score is 6.4 out of 10, which is Medium, close to High.

title: Chip makers moved more than the big AI users
text: The companies that build parts for AI jumped the most on Monday. TSMC rose 13.9%, Vertiv 12.1% and AMD 6.9%. The big companies that buy those parts moved less: Microsoft rose 1.6% and Amazon 3.5%. Stocks that go up fastest on good days usually fall fastest on bad days. That is why Vertiv (8.1) and AMD (7.7) have high risk scores, while Microsoft is at 3.9.

title: A December rate hike is still expected
text: The Federal Reserve meets on December 9. Traders still expect it to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percent. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, the highest in this chart. Higher rates make borrowing cost more, and that can weigh on fast growing companies.

title: Lesson 64: What is a gap at the open?
text: The stock market is closed overnight, but news keeps happening. So a stock can open at a very different price from where it closed. If it opens higher, that is a gap up. If it opens lower, that is a gap down. On Monday, NVIDIA opened far above Friday's close because the news about its CEO came out while the market was closed. Gaps remind us that you cannot always sell at the price you see on the screen the night before. That is one reason to keep any single stock a small part of what you own.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices, 52 week ranges and beta for all 17 names come from FMP at Monday's close (November 23). Analyst price targets are for NVDA, TSM, AMD, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, LMT and GE; company numbers like P/E are carried from the last update. The 10 year Treasury yield is a monthly average from Alpha Vantage, through October. Sector moves are averages of all NASDAQ listed stocks, so they can differ from the big index funds. News comes from company releases and news outlets, linked on each story. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell.
